candidates: When implementing a `reset()` method on a state-container class, prefer simple reassignment (`this.records = this.init()`) over in-place property deletion and reassignment. In-place mutation is only justified if external callers are explicitly known to hold a direct reference to the records object that must remain stable across resets.

Do not export utility or helper functions from production modules when those functions are only used in test files. Define such helpers in the test file itself or in a shared test-utility module, to avoid unnecessary code in the production bundle.

When broadening a TypeScript type annotation to accept additional input shapes (e.g., `string` to `string | string[]`), verify that all runtime consumers already handle the new shape correctly. A type-only change can compile without errors while runtime behavior remains unverified—check the actual implementation, not just the type signature.
Implement new stateful utility abstractions as ES6 classes rather than factory functions or closures, to match the standard JavaScript/TypeScript code style used throughout this project.

In TypeScript class definitions, use constructor parameter property shorthand (e.g., `constructor(private init: () => S)`) to declare and initialize class fields in one place, rather than declaring the property separately at the class level and manually assigning it in the constructor body.
